verdicts.fix: Careful: جَمَل (camel) and جَمِيل (beautiful) share the root letters j-m-l but are different words: don't mix them up.
verdicts.reason: جَمَل and جَمِيل are both under the root ج-م-ل in every dictionary; saying they come from different roots teaches a false root analysis in a course that teaches roots. The fix keeps the warning (two different words) and states the root correctly.

verdicts.scope: engine, one word (both vocalisations share the skeleton بجائزة); no content text changes
verdicts.reason: The problem is real but the cause is narrower than the reviewer says: cliticReading tests handGlossary first, and hand.json glosses بِجَائِزَةِ / بِجَائِزَة as 'a prize (fāza bi-: to win)', which does not start with '(with)', so the scoped '(with) the prize (of)' gloss is never consulted. Changing the general rule to read scoped glosses would make the reading depend on the place; the house-style precedent for a word the course writes as bi- + word whatever its gloss is CLITIC_FORCE (bi-khayr). The course's own glosses and note already write fāza bi-jāʾiza.

summary: Checked all 5 vocabulary-2 errors against audit/vocabulary.txt, content/glossary (hand.json, scoped.json, auto.json), the other audit areas where the words occur, and src/lang/ar/tap.ts (meaningChain, cliticReading, CLITIC_FORCE). 4 AGREE, 1 CHANGE, 0 DISAGREE.
